########## .docs/prd/regional.md — sections 4-5 ##########
| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB`                          | `/en-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC (REG-006 dom)      |
| EU domestic (FR) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `fr`                             | `/fr-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (IT) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `it`                             | `/it-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (ES) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `es`                             | `/es-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU international | `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                          | `/en-ch/`                      | EUR                    | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK               | `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                          | `/hk/`                         | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-007)      |
| ME               | `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                          | `/en-ae/`                      | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-008)      |

ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).

URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).

Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).

The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).

### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)

The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:

- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.

**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).

> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.

---

## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)

- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)

When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):

- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)

Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

---

## 3. Checkout Ownership

- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)

_For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md)._

---

## 4. Currency & Tax (REG-036 – REG-042)

- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).

---

## 5. EU Locale Billing Fields (REG-011)

The system will display locale-specific additional billing fields where required (e.g. Italian Codice Fiscale or VAT ID). **Open (REG-011):** confirm with Egaltine which other locales (e.g. Spanish NIF, French SIRET) require additional fields. Do not implement until confirmed.

---

## 6. Language & Translation (REG-044 – REG-047)

```ts
   *  keyboard focus before opening (e.g. mouse click) — without this Chakra falls back to
   *  document.body and AC10 focus-return fails. */
  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
  /** Element to focus when the drawer opens. Overrides Chakra's default (first focusable element
   *  in the panel, usually the close button) — use to land focus directly on the primary input. */
```

## 4. Locale / multi-site plumbing

### What a consumer can read

**`overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts` does not exist.** There is no override. Consumers import the base directly:

```ts
import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site';
```

— as at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:2`, `footer/index.tsx:6`, `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:4`, `recommended-products/index.tsx:136`.

**It ships untyped**, so the house pattern is a local cast. Two forms in use:

- `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:21-23`: `const { locale: siteLocale } = useMultiSite() as { locale?: { id: string } };` — with the comment *"useMultiSite ships untyped from the base SFCC package — same cast footer/index.tsx and useHeaderNav.ts already use."*
- `useCountryConfig.ts:4-7` declares a reusable `MultiSiteContext` type: `{ site?: {id, alias?}, locale?: {id, preferredCurrency?} }`.

It returns `{site, locale, buildUrl}` (`_app/index.tsx:172`).

**`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts:18-22`** is the ready-made bridge — returns the full `CountryConfig` for the active site+locale, keyed on `sfccSiteId` **and** `locale` to disambiguate the `en-GB` collision between UK and EU-English, falling back to AU. This is exactly what a mismatch detector needs, and it's Tier 4 (unlisted, plain squad ownership).

### The config chain

`config/sites.js` is a **merge of two files**, not a literal list (`config/sites.js:20-55`): `config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI-derived locale/currency, auto-generated) + `config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-maintained aliases + `sfccSiteId` override).

### EU Domestic — the answer to your specific question

**There is no single "EU Domestic site".** EU domestic is **four separate PWA sites**, each with exactly one locale, all backed by the one real SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`.

`config/sites.overlay.js:38-42`, verbatim:

```js
  // EU domestic — four single-locale PWA sites, all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr', alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it', alias: 'it-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es', alias: 'es-eu' }] },
```

`config/default.js:129-133`:

```js
      // EU domestic: one PWA site per locale prefix — all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU (see sites.js)
      ZimmermannEUen: 'en-eu',
      ZimmermannEUfr: 'fr-eu',
      ZimmermannEUit: 'it-eu',
      ZimmermannEUes: 'es-eu',
```

**So yes — `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` all exist in config**, but as **site aliases, not locale prefixes.** `config/default.js:70-78` sets `url.site: 'path'`, `url.locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`. Because each PWA site has exactly one locale and that locale is therefore its default (`sites.js:42`: `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`), `showDefaults:false` suppresses the locale segment — the URL carries the *site alias* only.

**This is the single most important structural consequence for SFCC-689: "switching language" is switching SITE, not switching locale.** `onSwitchLanguage(locale)` cannot be implemented as a locale change within one site. There is no `SITE_LOCALES` map anywhere in `config/` — I searched; the concept doesn't exist here.

`ZimmermannEU`'s SCAPI-supported locales (`config/sites.generated.js:77-104`): `en`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`. And `sites.js:34-42` carries a long comment explaining why `defaultLocale` deliberately ignores SCAPI's site-level default — *"BM's ZimmermannEU default 'en-GB' would wrongly apply to the EUfr/EUit/EUes PWA sites too, since all 4 share one real SFCC site."*

Locale→slug lookup, if you need the reverse direction: `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts:29-48` maps `en-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, en-GB, EUR}`, `fr-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, fr, EUR}`, `it-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, it, EUR}`, `es-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, es, EUR}`.

**Hook:** `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`.

Signature (`:12` inside `UiCopyContextValue`, hook at `:52`):

```ts
t: (key: string, fallback: string, values?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
isLoading: boolean;
```

```ts
export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
```

**No-Provider behaviour: degrades, never throws.** `FALLBACK_ONLY` at `:33-36` returns `interpolateUiCopy(fallback, values)`. `{token}` interpolation works identically with or without a Provider (`:21-24`). ## 6. Cookie / dismissal persistence — **no utility exists**

**There is no cookie utility anywhere in `overrides/`.** Grep for `document.cookie|setCookie|getCookie|js-cookie|cookies.set|cookies.get|expires=` across `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` returns **only four hits, all HTTP `Cache-Control` headers**: `overrides/app/ssr/slasTokens.ts:86`, `pages/home/index.tsx:122`, `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:238`, `pages/product-list/index.tsx:316`. Nothing writes a browser cookie.

**Nearest precedent is Web Storage, not cookies** — `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`. Worth reading for its defensive pattern: `:121` and `:127` pick `isRegistered ? localStorage : sessionStorage`, and `:30` documents *"browsing mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage` access, not just on write"* — Safari private mode throws on **read** too. Its test file covers both throw paths (`useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts:176, 191`). Any suppression-flag utility you write needs the same try/catch on read and write.

**`js-cookie` caveat.** It is present at `node_modules/js-cookie` but **only as a transitive dependency of `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`** (`node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/utils.js:13`, `.../auth/storage/cookie.js:7`). It is **not** in this repo's `package.json` — `Object.keys({...dependencies, ...devDependencies}).filter(/cookie/i)` returns `[]`. Importing it directly would mean depending on an undeclared transitive dep, and `.claude/rules/conventions.md` forbids importing from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths. Adding it needs integration-team approval (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7). A ~15-line hand-rolled `document.cookie` helper avoids both problems.

2. **Config-row comments carry the Figma node IDs and the reason a flag is moot** — e.g. `:441-444`.
3. **Per-variant recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig(RECIPE, {variant})`** — `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:186` is the pattern; `zimmDrawer.css.ts:137-199` the recipe shape.

**Runner-up precedent for the composition shape:** `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` — 95 lines, all logic in `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, body is `ZimmDrawer` + content organism + `finalFocusRef={triggerRef}` + `initialFocusRef`. That is structurally what your SFCC-689 consumer should look like.

### Canonical four-file pattern

Recipe key = PascalCase component name. Component folder = camelCase. Files:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/
  index.tsx                        ← component (named export matching folder)
  index.stories.tsx                ← Storybook
  index.test.tsx                   ← Vitest
  zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts         ← co-located recipe
  zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts    ← optional 5th: asserts recipe values
```

Organism example (4 files, no `.css.test.ts`):

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/
  index.tsx  ·  index.stories.tsx  ·  index.test.tsx  ·  zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts
```

**Two guard tests your new recipe must pass — both run on `npm run test`:**

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` — walks `overrides/app/components/**`, reconciles a recipe's declared `parts` against the `styles.<part>` reads in the sibling `index.tsx`. Its docblock (`:1-22`) explains the real mechanism: `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`, **not** `baseStyle`, so an undeclared part silently stops responding to variants. **Directly relevant to you: a two-variant recipe means an undeclared part will break on exactly one variant.**
- `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` — five guards. The one that will bite you is *"no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale"* (`:28-35`): `gap: 'm'` **fails the build**; you must write `gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-m)'`. Note the SCOPE caveat at `:38-45` — it cannot see the same mistake in a JSX/`sx` prop, so apply the discipline by hand there. Also run `npm run audit:tokens` (`package.json:76`) before the PR.

**Cross-file shared values** go in a small module in `theme/components/` — `zimmDrawerShared.ts` (12 lines, one exported constant) is the minimal reference; `footerShared.ts` the canonical one.

## 9. Theme registration

`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — 97 lines, dead simple: one named import per recipe (lines 1-47), one flat `components` export object (lines 48-97). Consumed by `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:18` (`import { components } from './components'`) and `:58` (`components,`).

Relevant lines, verbatim:

```ts
// :1
import { Button, ZimmButtonLabel } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css';
// :6
import { ZimmDrawer } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css';
// :9
import { ZimmPdpDrawer } from 'app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmPdpDrawer/zimmPdpDrawer.css';
// :40
import { ZimmProductCard } from 'app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css';

// :48-49, :55, :58, :89
export const components = {
  Button,
  ...
  ZimmDrawer,
  ...
  ZimmPdpDrawer,
  ...
  ZimmProductCard,
  ...
};
```

**Key-name conventions, all mechanically enforced:**
- The import path **drops the `.ts`** — `zimmDrawer.css`, not `zimmDrawer.css.ts`.
- The key is **PascalCase, `Zimm`-prefixed**. That prefix is not cosmetic: `recipeGuards.test.ts:20-24` explains that `theme/index.ts` composes with `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which **deep merges** — a recipe named `Footer` inherits SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it. Namespacing with `Zimm` is what prevents that.
- `Button` and `Header`/`ListMenu` are the deliberate exceptions — they *do* target Chakra/SFCC recipes.
- Chakra resolves by the **string** passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, so file location is purely organisational (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s co-location section).

Only 5 files remain in `theme/components/` itself: `index.ts`, `footerShared.ts`, `headerShared.ts`, `navConstants.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`, plus `recipeGuards.test.ts`. Everything else has moved to co-location.

## 10. Storybook + test conventions in practice

### Portal-rendered drawer story — `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`

`title: 'Elements/ZimmDrawer'` (`:9`). Imports test utils from **`'storybook/test'`** (`:4`) — not `@storybook/test`, not `@testing-library/user-event`.

The portal query, verbatim (`:32-40`):

```ts
  play: async () => {
    // Portal renders outside canvasElement — testing.md §Layer-2 exception. Chakra's Drawer is
    // built on its Modal primitive, which renders DrawerContent via a Portal by default, so
    // within(canvasElement) can't reach it.
    const doc = within(document.body);
    const dialog = await doc.findByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeInTheDocument();
    await expect(dialog).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'Example drawer');
  },
```

This is the **only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`** per `.claude/rules/testing.md` — and the comment citing the exception is mandatory.

Three more conventions from this file:

- **Close assertions must `waitForElementToBeRemoved`, not `queryByRole`** (`:69-73`): *"Chakra's Drawer plays a slide-out exit transition (framer-motion) before AnimatePresence actually unmounts the dialog node — an immediate `queryByRole('dialog')` assertion here catches it mid-animation, still present with a near-100% translateX."* **Your dismiss/CTA-closes-drawer stories will hit this.**
- **Stateful stories need a named component**, not an inline `render: () => { useState(...) }` (`:19-28`) — a lowercase `render` can't call hooks.
- **Assert the accessible name, not the mechanism** (`:94-97`): `findByRole('dialog', {name: 'SIGN IN'})` rather than pinning to `aria-labelledby` vs `aria-label`. Ideal for your per-variant accessible-name AC.

Story categorisation for your component: `.claude/rules/components.md` gives `Layout/` for *"Global chrome, navigation, and structural components"*. A country/language mismatch prompt is global chrome, not commerce — so `Layout/CountryLanguageMismatch`. `ZimmDrawer` itself sits in `Elements/`.

### Organism `index.test.tsx` — what gets mocked

The canonical reference (cited by name in `.claude/rules/testing.md`) is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx`. It mocks exactly four things, each with a written justification:

1. **`ZimmIcon`** — mandatory, not optional (`:11-16`):
   ```ts
   // ZimmIcon pulls in the base SFCC icons barrel, which throws under Vitest (SVG imports
   // resolve to raw path strings here). No assertion below depends on an icon's own content.
   vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({
     ZimmIcon: (props: { 'aria-label'?: string; 'aria-hidden'?: boolean }) => (
       <span aria-label={props['aria-label']} aria-hidden={props['aria-hidden']} />
     ),
   }));
   ```
   This is a known, documented harness gap (`.claude/rules/testing.md` § Mocking). The fix is Tier 1 (`vitest.config.ts`) so it can't be fixed properly. **Note the variant that forwards props** rather than returning `null` — use that when an assertion depends on an accessible name.
2. **The child organism/modal** (`:24-38`) — stubbed to a minimal `role="dialog"` with mock buttons.
3. **Its own hook** (`:40-46`) — `vi.mock('app/hooks/useSubscribeSection', () => ({useSubscribeSection: vi.fn()}))`, with the reasoning at `:39-43`: *"Mocking it here isolates this suite to ZimmSubscribeSection's own contract: given a state, does it render the right branch, and does it correctly wire DOM events into the hook's handlers."*
4. **`useUiCopy`** (`:49-55`) — *"Default matches the no-Provider fallback behaviour real callers see."*

**For a drawer specifically**, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx:9-26` shows the ZimmDrawer stub:

```ts
vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer', () => ({
  ZimmDrawer: ({ isOpen, onClose, children }: {...}) =>
    isOpen ? (
      <div role="dialog">
        <button onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
        {children}
      </div>
    ) : null,
}));
```

Plus `useMultiSite` — it ships as `.js` containing JSX that Vitest can't parse (`uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:17-19`), so **any test touching it must mock it**, always with a factory:

```ts
vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site', () => ({ default: vi.fn() }));
```

`.claude/rules/testing.md` is explicit that a mocked-out child does **not** excuse skipping your own test file — scope what you assert, don't skip the file.

## Things I'd flag before you plan

1. **`onSwitchLanguage(locale)` is the wrong signature for this codebase.** Switching EU language = switching **PWA site** (`ZimmermannEUfr` etc.), not switching locale within one site — see §4. `config/default.js:129-133` + `config/sites.overlay.js:38-42` are the proof. `buildUrl()` from `useMultiSite` may not do what SFCC-831 assumes; verify before the API is frozen, because SFCC-689 is the only consumer and the shape will be hard to change later.

2. **PRD says "modal", the story says "drawer".** `.docs/prd/regional.md:71-73`: *"show a language mismatch **modal**"* (REG-029/031); `:64`: *"a country **slide-out** is shown"* (REG-015). The story specifies a right-anchored drawer for both. AGENTS.md's Doc-integrity rule says pause and cite rather than pick silently — `.docs/prd/regional.md:71` (REG-029) is the line to cite. Note `ZimmModal` also exists (`ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/`) if the PRD wins for the language variant.

3. **PRD's language-mismatch trigger is GEO-IP country, not browser language.** `.docs/prd/regional.md:73` (REG-029/030): *"When a user's **GEO-IP country** doesn't match the URL language"*, with the mapping France/Monaco→FR, Italy/San Marino→IT, Spain→ES. SFCC-689 as described triggers on **browser language** (EN/FR/IT/ES). These are different signals with different accuracy and different privacy profiles, and only one of them is in the confirmed PRD. Same doc-integrity pause applies.

4. **Nothing in the repo can supply an IP-detected country today.** `request-processor.js` is the untouched stub, `worker/main.js` is empty, and there is no geo header plumbing anywhere (§3). `COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE` (`countries.ts:128`) is a lookup table with no data source behind it and zero consumers. SFCC-831's `location-prompt` variant can be built and story-tested against props, but **SFCC-689's real trigger has an unbuilt server-side dependency that lands in a Tier 1-elect file.** Worth surfacing as a dependency, not discovering mid-build.

5. **`overrides/app/components/global/` does not exist** and contradicts the `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` convention every component since PR #85 follows. Resolve the path before scaffolding.

6. **Didomi is entirely unbuilt** (§6), and the DNT placeholder modal that E2E used to rely on was removed by SFCC-863. There is no consent signal to gate a cookie on.

7. **`zimmDrawer` has no unit test**, and `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx:9` asserts in a comment that it does. If your a11y ACs (focus trap, focus return, dialog semantics) are meant to be *proven* rather than inherited, the only existing evidence is story `play`s. Given the `.runs`-recorded "prove, don't assert" standard, consider whether the focus-return path — which has a real documented gotcha at `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:193-197` — needs a test that's been made to fail on purpose.
